title: Tackling Instance-Dependent Label Noise with Class Rebalance and Geometric Regularization

problem.claim: Instance-dependent label noise complicates accurate transition-matrix identification and creates identifiability challenges without stringent assumptions.

gap.claim: Existing transition-matrix estimation methods can be distorted by inter-class imbalance and by selecting mostly unambiguous intra-class instances as confident clean examples.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces the Class Rebalance and Geometric Regularization-based Framework (CRGR).
CRGR uses smoothed, noise-tolerant reweighting to balance inter-class representation and reduce overfitting to dominant classes.
CRGR regularizes transition-matrix learning by aligning it with feature-space similarity, thereby incorporating ambiguous instances into training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets.
The authors report that CRGR outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods and significantly improves classification accuracy on the evaluated datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Accurate transition-matrix identification is important, but instance-dependent noise creates identifiability challenges.
Existing methods estimate transition matrices by extracting confident clean instances with neural networks.
Class imbalance and selection bias toward unambiguous intra-class instances can distort the inferred noise patterns.
CRGR addresses these biases through class rebalance, noise-tolerant reweighting, and geometric regularization based on feature similarity.
The authors report improved robustness, generalization, and classification accuracy relative to existing methods in synthetic and real-world experiments.

source_observation.claim: Instances with similar features are described as often exhibiting parallel noise patterns, motivating alignment between the transition matrix and feature-space similarity.

interpretation.claim: Representing local geometric relationships may help include ambiguous examples in noise-model training.

application.claim: Use feature-space similarity as a regularization signal when ambiguous instances are informative about structured label noise.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that feature similarity tracks noise similarity across all datasets or feature representations.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical effect sizes.
The abstract does not state the assumptions, computational cost, or implementation details of CRGR.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported experimental superiority.
